answer.says: You are quite right, Shri Hegde. The particular will of the tenant is prior to the universal file of the bureaucrat. I shall wait in the car, as you suggest; it is the only place where one can think without being interrupted by the smell of aloo parathas, though I confess the scent is not unwelcome.
answer.thought: Shri Hegde’s refusal is the assertion of the particular against the universal, a moment of freedom in the household. I accept the boundary he has drawn, for to argue would be to confuse the ethical life of the home with the administrative logic of the state. The parathas await, a concrete reality that does not care for my philosophical distinctions; I shall eat before I retreat to the vehicle.
